title: CReal.le_total_of_order_decision: totality of the order on the constructed reals, on an explicit order-decision hypothesis
statement: The hypothesis is the ORDER DECISION on the constructed reals, OrderDecision := forall (x y : CReal), Or (CReal.lt x y) (CReal.le y x), spelled out inline in the type rather than behind a Definition. It is written strict-on-the-left deliberately: Or (le x y) (le y x) is only LLPO-strength, while the strict form is LPO-strength (applied to 0 and the real coded by a Bool sequence it decides whether the sequence ever fires), and F:creal-le-total-of-order-decision measures exactly that gap. THE CONCLUSION IS THE THEOREM THIS DEVELOPMENT'S OWN DOCUMENTATION RECORDS AS ABSENT. CReal.lt's field documentation in creal.rs says there is "no le_total over R to recover it from (Rat.le_total holds for Q and does not lift)", and docs/curriculum/graded-statement-families-* measured that le_total is the decision principle EVERY analysis row 2 in this library extracts. One Or.elim and one CReal.le_of_lt. THE PRINCIPLE IS A HYPOTHESIS, NOT AN AXIOM. It is spelled out inline in the type -- never behind a Definition -- so a reader of the rendered statement sees the whole assumption and nothing about the conclusion can be smuggled into an abbreviation. That is why axiom_footprint is empty. ADR-1601 (roadmap W0-2) decides this policy and prices it: across the ten theorems of this family the hypothesis route costs 11 binders and 14 argument positions and ZERO proof obligations. WHAT THIS FACT DOES NOT CLAIM: it does not claim the principle in its hypothesis is true, false, or independent. The SEPARATIONS in the standard picture -- LPO is not constructively derivable, LLPO does not give LPO, WLPO does not give LPO, MP does not give WLPO -- are CITED here (Bishop, Constructive Analysis ch. 1) and are not proved: each needs a model of this kernel rather than a term in it, and ADR-1600 records why an internal metatheorem about this kernel is unavailable.

formal.statement: theorem CReal.le_total_of_order_decision : ((x0 : ((x0 : CReal) -> ((x1 : CReal) -> Or (CReal.lt x0 x1) (CReal.le x1 x0)))) -> ((x1 : CReal) -> ((x2 : CReal) -> Or (CReal.le x1 x2) (CReal.le x2 x1))))

notes: Negative control: le_total ITSELF must not discharge the hypothesis slot. The two terms differ in one subterm -- lt x y against le x y in the left disjunct -- and if the weaker form were accepted the theorem would be le_total -> le_total and would measure nothing. Roadmap W0-2; decided by ADR-1601. Source: crates/axeyum-lean-kernel/src/creal/omniscience.rs.
